title: Program calendar for quarterly roadmap synchronization and cutover roles
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Goal: Produce a program-level launch calendar that links roadmap milestones, OKR checkpoints, and concrete cutover/rollback ownership for runtime, console, and API surfaces. The calendar will annotate capacity guardrails, blackout windows, decision checkpoints (go/no-go), and downstream customer-facing communications windows. Deliverables:
- A single canonical calendar (CSV + Confluence page) that product, eng, design, and SRE can subscribe to.
- A decision checklist for 'week-of-go' used by release owners.
- Ownership matrix mapping feature slices to runtime/console/API owners and on-call escalation contacts.
- Capacity annotations per launch (estimated GPU-hours, reserved Dedicated lanes, regional fallback plan).
Why this matters: multiple launches in the same quarter historically collided on capacity and overlapping rollouts. This program calendar reduces risk by making capacity and cutover decisions explicit and traceable to OKR milestones.
comments: 2026-02-12: Kickoff with Eng (runtime infra), Console PM, and SRE. Agreed to use a CSV-backed canonical calendar and a Confluence summary page. Action: Eng to provide capacity estimate template by 2026-02-19. - Aisha

2026-02-19: Runtime team delivered capacity-template PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/infra/PR-2846. Template includes expected token/sec, GPU-hours, burst profile. Not final — needs Console and API owners to fill in for first-pass launches. - Diego

2026-02-26: First pass calendar populated for three planned launches. Identified conflict: two high-capacity runtime rollouts target same regional Dedicated pool in the same week. Trade-off discussed: shift non-critical console UI launch by one sprint vs reserve extra Dedicated lanes (cost impact). Logged for leadership review. - Aisha

2026-03-04: Leadership recommends shifting console UI release to avoid cost spike. Updated calendar and notified stakeholders via #launch-calendar Slack channel. Added canary ramp signals to decision checklist. - Diego

2026-03-10: Added postmortem learnings from December incident (inc-2025-12-runtime-throttle) to the calendar as a risk annotation for any multi-model rollouts. Plan to require an SLO smoke-test during canary for all runtime-impacting launches. - SRE
